div.head: II As 2
div.ab: Be lafordleasum mannum. And we cwædon be ðam hlafordleasum mannum, ðe nan man nan riht ætbegytan ne mæg, þæt man bude ðære mægðe, þæt hi hine to rihte gehamette ⁊ him hlaford fundon on folcgemote.
Ond we cwædon be þam hlafordleasan mannum, ðe mon nán ryht ætbegytan ne mæg, þæt mon beode ðære mægþe, ðæt hi hine to folcryhte gehamette ⁊ him hlaford finden on folcgemote.
⁊ we cwædon be ðam hlafordleasum mannum, þe mon nan riht ætbegitan ne mæg, þæt mon bude þær mæg, þæt heo hine to ryht gehamette ⁊ him hlaford finde ⁊ folcgemote.
Et diximus de illis qui dominos non habent, de quibus rectum difficile conquiritur aut nullum, ut precipiatur cognationi eorum, ut eos ad rectum adducat et dominum eis inueniant in conuentu publico.

[Be lafordleasum mannum.] [B] Ond we cwædon be þam hlafordleasan mannum, ðe mon nán ryht ætbegytan ne mæg, þæt mon beode ðære mægþe, ðæt hi hine to folcryhte gehamette ⁊ him hlaford finden on folcgemote.

With regard to lordless men from whom no [legal] satisfaction can be obtained, we have delared that their relatives shall be commanded to settle them in a fixed residence where they will become amenable to public law, and find them a lord at a public meeting.

Concerning lordless men. And we pronounced about those lordless men, from whom no justice can be obtained, that one should order their kindred to fetch back such a person to justice and to find him a lord in public meeting.

(Von herrenlosen Leuten. B) Und wir bestimmten über solche herrenlosen Leute, von denen sich keine Rechtserfüllung erlangen lässt, dass man der Sippe [derselben] gebiete, dass sie einen solchen fürs (ordentliche H) Gericht sesshaft mache, und [sie] sollen ihm in der Volksversammlung einen Herrn ausfindig machen.

(Of lordless men. B) And we determined concerning those lordless men from whom no legal satisfaction can be obtained, that the kindred [of the same] be commanded to settle such a one at home for the (regular, H) court, and [they] are to find him a lord at the public assembly.
div.note: So reads ‘⁊ folcgemote’; Liebermann would correct to ‘on’.

gehamettan has been assumed from this context and from its etymology to mean “to domicile”, but one should compare the O.E. version of the Capitula of Theodulf (ed. A.S.Napier (1916), pp. 115f.), where the words omnes debitores uestros repetitis (Douai version: “you exact of all your debtors”) of Isaiah lviii. 3, are rendered ealle eowre gyltendras ge hametað. A rendering “bring back”, or “bring home” would suit very well the only other recorded instance, i.e. Birch, No. 599; he moste a inberðan menn hamettan to Eblesburnan, “he might bring home to Ebblesbourne the persons born on the estate”.
